sources.note: Compresses a safety guard's textual rationales into continuous latent states by a staged curriculum, cutting 268 reasoning tokens to 1.60 and latency 8.9-fold, and adds an on-demand decoder that reconstructs a human-readable audit artifact — whose own ablation shows the artifact is anchored far more by the source text than by the latent states it is supposed to inspect.
sources.title: LatentGuard: Efficient and Inspectable Latent Reasoning for LLM Safeguards

sources.note: Splits a video model's latent computation into perception latents that always ground the question in visual evidence and reasoning latents allocated only when the question needs inference, and shows that reasoning latents without rationale supervision are worse than no reasoning latents at all.
sources.title: Perception Before Reasoning: Dynamic Latent Reasoning for Video Understanding and Question Answering

sources.note: Bolts a small trainable recurrent block between a frozen 1.1B language model's body and its output head, so reasoning happens as repeated refinement of two latent vectors rather than as generated tokens.
sources.title: Think Deep, Speak Once: Relit, A Recursive Latent Implicit Transformer Framework

sources.note: Combines in-context learning through evolving recurrent memory with iterative reasoning in a continuous latent workspace that is never decoded into language, reaching 29.5% pass@2 on public ARC-AGI-1 at $0.0007 per task from 150M parameters, and then probes with controlled tasks what the resulting demonstration-bound operators can and cannot do.
sources.title: BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning

sources.note: Tests the claim that continuous chain-of-thought lets a model hold several candidate solutions at once, and finds it holds only for models trained from scratch: off-the-shelf models collapse a superposed input to a single token within a few layers, and fine-tuned latent reasoners solve the task in one forward pass and copy the answer through the latent slots.
sources.title: The Illusion of Superposition? A Principled Analysis of Latent Thinking in Language Models

sources.note: Explains why latent chain-of-thought excels at exploration but fails at computation by identifying decisional certainty as the governing variable, formalizing it as the Symbolic Index, and proving that curriculum learning is not merely helpful but necessary for training latent reasoners.
sources.title: Capabilities and Fundamental Limits of Latent Chain-of-Thought

result.definition: Feeding a model's last hidden state back as the next input embedding so that reasoning proceeds in continuous space rather than through emitted tokens, and across 6 sources the reference implementation of latent reasoning -- along with the archive's clearest evidence about what such methods do and do not achieve. Its measured trade is domain-dependent: on grade-school arithmetic explicit chain of thought reaches 42.9 percent at 25.0 tokens against its 34.1 at 8.2, while on a structured logic task it reaches 97.0 percent at 14.2 tokens against explicit chain of thought's 77.5 at 49.4 -- so it wins where search over a constrained space is the bottleneck and loses where the reasoning is arithmetic. Two negative results matter more. It is fragile to train: removing the curriculum collapses it to at or below the no-reasoning baseline on two of three tasks. And in the fine-tuned regime its latent tokens can be inert -- deleting every one of them changes accuracy by at most 1.0 point across four models, with entity probing showing the final answer dominating the belief distribution from step 0 with no progression, against a discrete baseline where the target takes over only at the last step.
